newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end mixed in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end mixed in slow trade.

text.p: The Australian share market ended mixed on Monday, losing ground in late trade as investors focussed on negative sentiment surrounding metal prices and the local currency.
Having scaled fresh heights early, the thinly-dealt market tumbled back just as quickly as the miners were mauled on concerns over commodity prices and the Australian dollar.
The All Ordinaries index lost 0.3 points to 2,446.4 after hitting an intraday and record high of 2,461.9, surpassing the previous record of 2,456.7 on January 20.

"I was bullish this morning and that was borne out by the early events but the major resources stocks led it down in the afternoon," said broker Kevin Lourey of Melbourne-based broker Peake Lands Kirwan.
"It would appear the market is not so sure about the strength of our dollar and also about commodity prices."
Other players echoed similar sentiments about a start that promised so much but failed to deliver.
"It came right off the top after running hard early," said a Sydney-based dealer, adding that only modest investor interest had made it difficult to convincingly capture the early heights.
"There was not much trade though and not enough interest to keep it at the higher levels. Many are still waiting to see the upcoming profit results," he said.
Miner CRA underpinned the market's early ascent and held most of its gains to limit the day's overall losses. Its shares closed 36 cents higher at A$18.94 (US$14.39).

Other resource stocks failed to fare as well. Major oil producers Woodside Petroleum and Santos Ltd came under pressure from the sharp fall in the oil price with both their shares closing about 2.5 percent lower at A$9.40 and A$4.71 respectively.

In the industrials, the banks continued to be the feature and Commonwealth Bank the star player. Its shares closed 12 cents higher at A$13.58 after reaching a record high of A$13.78 on profit expectations from its half year results due Wednesday, its continuing yield attraction and persistent speculation about a special dividend.
Major brewing group Foster's Brewing closed 11 cents lower at A$2.54 despite a 13 percent higher first half pre-tax operating profit of A$184.8 million.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about 10 to nine, while about 30 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
